summary: A Claude seat on an auto install starts in a workspace that has a .mcp.json; before, it stopped at an approval dialog and its channel never attached

replay.detail: No stored history or replay change.

schema.detail: No database, claim or configuration schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: Claude asks 'New MCP server found in .mcp.json' for each project server that is not in the project's enabledMcpjsonServers. --dangerously-skip-permissions skips the dialog and --permission-mode auto does not, so a seat moved from bypass to auto stopped at it before any MCP server connected: the st channel never attached, mail was held, and the seat showed claude-channel-unattached. When st admits a seat's workspace (the same step that accepts the workspace trust dialog) it now also adds the servers named in that workspace's .mcp.json to the project's enabledMcpjsonServers in the seat's Claude config. A server the project lists in disabledMcpjsonServers stays disabled, an unreadable .mcp.json approves nothing, and other fields are kept. This is the approval a bypass seat already had, for the servers present at launch; a server added later is approved at the next launch. Claude approves by name: once a name is enabled, a later edit to that server's command in .mcp.json runs without another dialog, which is code execution from repository content under the trust the workspace's project hooks already have, so a workspace holding untrusted content (a fork's branch checked out for review) must not be a seat workspace; the same goes for any workspace that holds someone else's branch or fork. Each approval is logged by the driver with the server name and a hash of its definition.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the dialog for auto-mode seats whose workspace has a .mcp.json.
